Preface this by saying I am playing on Linux, so some of the performance issues may be related.

Without knowing much about the history of it, this game feels like its trying to fit that Capital Ship + Boarding Fantasy, something which I feel has very much been missing since the original Battlefront games. That part of it is actually pretty great, the capital ships, boarding, all are pretty cool when they work together. I think the bot support is pretty decent as well, and considering the game is practically dead online (literally 0 players online) save for a few community organized events, this seems like a good move.

I'd say the biggest problems for me are optimization and more specifically CPU usage. Maybe it's the engine, but it seems to be quite single threaded and does not make use of the CPU well. I'm on a 7840u, which is a laptop processor, but only goes to about 20% usage in this game, and feels like the bottleneck as the gpu does appear to be being used properly.

I also think that the infantry combat is quite poor. Handheld weapons feel pretty janky, weightless, and the animations are pretty barebones, and don't showcase the game's strengths very well. I don't really know why there were added, unless a space tie in was planned at some point.

The layered objectives are also kinda boring IMO. I've seen this in EA battlefront and never liked it. You'll be in a space battle at one point, then be fighting on the ground the next. Oddly though, you're spaceships still kind of hang around, spawnable, and operateable. There's just nothing happening because everyone is aboard the station. I got kind of confused by this at one point, because all the objective markers disapeared, leaving me to meander around for a few minutes until I realized where the objective was by opening up the redeploy screen.

Why am I still giving it a thumbs up? Because it's closer to fulfilling what the original battlefront games started, and I hope that if there is any development runway left I would like to see the following:

- Performance pass, specifically on CPU usage.
- Handheld weapon animations are pretty rough, and since it's what the player is looking at 90% of the time, would be nice to give them a bit more weight. Kind of on the player controller side as well.
- Making some of the more linear, staged modes, a bit more dynamic and replayable. 
- Would be amazing if all had indoor and outdoor battle objectives running at the same time. 'd take just allowing the order of objectives to be randomized, or allowing players to reset them.

This probably will never be seen by the devs, and I imagine it would be too much work at this point in the game's lifecycle, but I digress, those are my thoughts.

Best sci-fi combined arms game nobody has heard of. The on ground combat is like battlefield, then the space combat is like the classic battlefront games done MUCH better (no offense battlefront 2, everyone still loves you).

The ground combat combined arms gameplay done with the 64 player format makes you forget you aren't playing battlefield very quickly, the maps aren't empty either (looking at you 2042), and there's an obvious ton of effort put into the maps by the developers. The ONLY complaint I can think about is the questionable progression system, where you start the game with everything available to you, but in order to equip more of the best gear you need to level up one of three XP paths in order to get more supply points (just because you can equip the best armor doesn't mean you can equip the best weapons or gear with that armor, good luck killing AIA with your bare hands).

The space combat has very little to complain about, if anything. Being able to punch a big enough hole into a ship, then fly into that hole with a dropship to create a spawn point so you can then destroy the ship from the inside out is ridiculously fun, even more fun when you destroy the core and you have a 1 minute timer to escape the ship before it explodes with everyone in it, fighting your way to the hangar is something you only see in singleplayer campaign settings. The space missions also translate into ground combat from time to time, which is a nice touch (albeit not planetside ground combat, just on stations and asteroids, still, you can only expect so much).

The fact that this game has not been made more popular is criminal. And while the devs are still pumping out updates with a 1.0 release on the way, it's an absolute shame knowing that this game could have had so much more if it were more widely known.

Not that I think this takes away from the game at all, but one thing I frequently think about, as it is why I found this game at all, is Dust 514 on the old PS3, connected to the EVE universe where battles had a tangible impact on the overall EVE universe. This game does have a barebones faction system, the ULA vs the AIA, and it would be really cool if this game got more publicity than it did if they had some kind of overarching galaxy status determined by what faction the player chose to support out of game (obviously you can't always control what faction you get if the server is full in game). This does seem impractical given the lack of support the game has gotten but I am writing that out for everyone who passed this game up, we could have had a real one here, its your fault. Love you devs.

This game has unbelievable potential; The array and variety of interesting and fun weapons, all available from the start, ensure that the player may fulfill any of a variety of roles that suit their fancy any given time. The leveling system is rewarding, allowing budget increases to loadouts in three categories, which further increases customization options. The customization options themselves are extensive, with the changes that the player may make to their weapons, vehicles and gear often being quite palpable. The maps are not only visually amazing, but also well designed and fleshed out with details that fit perfectly into gameplay experience. The bots are humanlike and make for satisfying opponents to slay, and when multiple humans are on the same team against bots, the bot team's respawn rate increases. I quite enjoy this in the sense that the game can be played as a sort of tactical co-op bot slaying shooter fest. It absolutely flabbergasts me that this game does not have more active players, and if you are reading this, THIS GAME IS WORTH EVERY PENNY.
In a gaming industry oversaturated with soulless gray slop, Angels Fall First sits humbly as a hidden, beautifully polished gem in the rough, just waiting to be discovered and adored. This game has an abundance of heart and soul. I have not seen one single microtransaction. I have not been offered a single pay-to-win mechanic. There is no subscription, no outside service to join. Just a shooter that's easy to pick up, feels good to play, with cool sci-fi weapons and engaging, nuanced gameplay. To the Devs, I salute you, and I thank you for making this game. Keep at it, and don't give up. This game is already amazing and worth the money at the time of review. I sincerely look forward to seeing what it will become in the future, and I will do anything I can to help this game grow.

This game can be summed up in one word. FRUSTRATING.

I couldn't even finish my second match because the game was so frustrating to play. Things from terrible Bloom on weapons, incompetent vehicle AI, to truly head scratching game design leaves this game to be such a frustrating experience.

- Bloom on weapons is EGREGIOUS. Games should reward you leading your shots well and good aiming but not this game. Bloom will make sure if you're not barrel stuffing the enemy, have fun watching your shots go all over the place, rarely hitting your target.

- Lack of ammo. This game is so bad at giving you ammo to fight with. Every life I had was the constant problem of having barely any ammo to fight with. About 90% of my lives ended with me running around with a knife because of how pathetic an amount of ammo you are given for all your weapons.

- Health/Ammo packs are LIMITED! What brain dead dev thought this was ok? Why on earth would you limit players to only being able to put down three health/ammo packs before not being able to put down anymore? This is incredibly stupid and this right here almost made me quit within the first 5 minutes of playing this game when I quickly found this out. Absolutely brain dead game design. It quickly got to the point just like in my previous ammo comment that I was FORCED to run around with just a knife because I wasn't around any teammates to give me ammo, and I was either out of the "ammo" to place down more health/ammo packs or naturally with a class that didn't have them. So, so stupid.

- Giving commands is impossible. My only squadmate (was never in a full squad for some reason) kept spamming me to give them orders but anytime I opened the map to do so, it's like the game ignored what I was doing. I kept clicking on him and nothing happened. Pressing the C key to issue orders was bare bones and terribly done. I can't just look at an objective and tell him to go there. It's really poorly done here.

- Creating a class is a joke. You have to balance THREE DIFFERENT BARS. Something like combat level, support level, and something else. Adding/changing anything to your class effects these 3 bars, making it an absolute infuriating experience just trying to customize your class. Really terrible game design. Again, it's like the devs of this game tried to make such simple things as frustrating as possible.

Недооценённая игра, содержащая в себе кучу интересных механик и возможностей. Создатели игры напрямую указывали, что вдохновлялись режимом Assault из Unreal Tournament-а, и это заметно.
Интересное:
- Куча-куча всяких разных пушек от пистолетиков до плазменных снайперок
- В целом довольно глубокая система экипировки персонажа, техники, самолётов, космических кораблей
- Разнообразие техники от обычных багги до сверхтяжёлых крейсеров на космических миссиях
- На вышеупомянутых космо-миссиях есть возможность абордажа кораблей. 
- Ничего не надо открывать, вся экипировка доступна с самого начала игры, так что экспериментировать можно бесконечно.
Минусы:
- Для своей картинки очень посредственная производительность даже на серверах, где все просчёты идут не на вашем компьютере. Но в целом играбельно даже на средненьких компьютерах с железом десятилетней давности.
- Мёртвый онлайн. Несмотря на 24/7 наличие официальных серверов (Сервера бывают неофициальные и вообще играть можно просто с ботами в соло), игроки приходят и уходят, что не приводит к появлению критической массы игроков для поднятия стабильного онлайна. Со стабильным онлайном игра ультра весёлая, что было доказано хрен знает сколько лет назад, когда игра случайно попала на главную страницу стима.
- Достаточно умные боты чтобы  не заскучать без игроков.

I am looking forward to the release of 1.0 , when people will (re) discover this fantastic game. I have been playing more regularly since the latest major update and let me tell you - This is a briliant achievement on the Unreal Engine 3, and gets more fun the more time you put into it (the huge array odf weapons, vehicles and options can be disorienting at first).

While multiplayer servers are mostly dormant as of yet, the NPCs are surprisingly adept and provide lots of challenge (both enemy and your team is capable) the territories game type is great but the incursion types (objective based assaults written around a story setting) are the best.

Angels Fall First has lots of personality and I dare to say even though its graphical engine has one or two generations wide gap between its contemporary peers, art direction is still one of the best I have seen in this kind of sci fi combined arms game.

Sure not perfect as it is early acces when I write it, but there are lots to praise here.
The maps are unique locations with exciting design and nice fine details, map flow is great, the CQC land warfare works well, your kit is highly modular and upgradable. Weapons and vehicles are also well thought out. Music is great and honestly the game surprises me with its features time and time again, especially in the incursion game type. Boarding an enemy station or spaceship while the space battle is raging outside never gets old!

Hats of for the indie devs, I really hope people will rediscover Angels Fall First and its rich lore, locations, its exciting spin on combined arms warfare.
